items.problem: Migrated NavigationView + Frame shell renders but the scenario content Frame is blank on every page; no scenario controls exist and every Launch invoke fails. Score 0/3.
items.evidence: migration-score.json (all 3 features fail, 'WinUI content frame blank; nav item selects but no page content'); source MainPage.xaml.cs SelectionChanged casts args.SelectedItem to NavigationViewItem while MenuItemsSource binds Scenario data items.
items.skill_search: grepped SKILL.md + MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md for NavigationView, MenuItemsSource, SelectedItem, SelectionChanged, Frame.Navigate, MenuItemTemplate
items.wrong_text_if_any: SKILL.md line 96 maps 'MainPage + ListView + Frame (SDK-sample idiom)' -> 'NavigationView + Frame' but no wiring pattern exists anywhere; MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md has RootFrame.Navigate for the root shell only, nothing for NavigationView item selection -> content Frame navigation.
items.root_cause: Skill directs migration to the NavigationView + Frame idiom (the single LLM-judgement shell decision) but ships no concrete wiring code. The dev-agent invented wiring with the classic type mismatch: with MenuItemsSource, SelectionChanged's args.SelectedItem is the bound DATA item, not a NavigationViewItem, so the cast fails and ScenarioFrame.Navigate is never called. Failure is silent (no build/runtime error).
items.proposed_fix: Add a 'NavigationView + Frame wiring (SDK-sample scenario list)' subsection to MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md with a copy-pasteable snippet that (1) navigates off the data item when MenuItemsSource is used (`args.SelectedItem is Scenario s`), or off item.Tag when literal NavigationViewItems are used; (2) performs the initial navigation from the source collection, not NavView.MenuItems; (3) calls a short falsifiable check: 'after selecting the first item, the content Frame must contain scenario controls'. Cross-link it from the SKILL.md shell-mapping table row.
items.generalizes: Nearly every UWP SDK sample uses the MainPage + ListView + Frame scenario-list idiom, and the skill explicitly steers all of them to NavigationView + Frame. The MenuItemsSource<->SelectedItem type trap and the empty-MenuItems initial-selection trap are the default mistakes for this idiom, so a correct wiring pattern prevents blank-content-frame failures across the whole SDK-sample family.
